page: Vultr voc-s-16c-128gb-2560s-amd is an Optimized Cloud Compute server instance featuring 16 dedicated vCPUs powered by AMD EPYC processors running at 2.0 GHz. Built on the x86_64 architecture, this configuration provides 8 physical cores with 2 threads per core. It is equipped with 128.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. Storage is bundled with a local 2560 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. No GPU accelerators are present on this model.

Benchmark data reveals strong memory performance, with large-block uncached write memory bandwidth ranking in the top tier (top 10%) and large-block uncached read bandwidth in the strong tier (top 25%). The Passmark memory score also registers in the top 25%. In contrast, compute performance is more moderate; stress-ng single-core CPU performance is strong, but multi-core CPU performance, Passmark CPU scores, and bzip3 decompression speeds fall into the average range. Database operations, Redis SET performance, and static web serving throughput similarly align with average tier expectations.

From a resource density perspective, this instance offers a favorable balance of high memory capacity and fast NVMe storage relative to its compute allocation. The dedicated AMD EPYC cores ensure consistent execution without CPU steal, though the 2.0 GHz base clock speed represents a tradeoff for workloads requiring high single-threaded compute velocity. The combination of top-tier memory write speeds and generous NVMe storage makes it a cost-efficient option for memory-intensive and data-heavy deployments that do not require GPU acceleration.

This server configuration is well-suited for hosting relational and non-relational databases, in-memory caching layers such as Redis, and medium-scale data processing pipelines. The high memory capacity also supports virtualized environments, enterprise web applications, and moderate LLM inference tasks using smaller models.
